blocks.x: PROCEEDINGS

This time it will be in a different way, if I get to it at all. But I was thinking, coming up here, you've got a career as a leader and as a bass virtuoso and as a composer. Do you think of all that as a whole, or is there one of the three that's most important to you?
Composing.
Why?
I enjoy it more. (Inaudible) enjoy playing a whole lot.
Yeah. You say, you didn't enjoy playing a whole lot.
I did when I was younger.
Yeah.
That's when the guys used to have battles, go out to somebody. There's no more jam sessions.
There haven't been jam sessions for, I guess, at least -- what, 20, 30 years?
At least.
Why did the jam sessions kind of disappear?
Well, see, the agents for booking jam sessions (inaudible). They were trying to accomplish what was going on in jam sessions. Before that, there was guys
working in the big bands, travelling around. And they would get together because (inaudible) find someplace to play, to get a release from the tensions of reading music.
Yeah.
That's how jazz (inaudible) came about.
And then as they began to really book them as jam sessions, they weren't jam sessions anymore.
No more.
It's like Norman Granz, he jazz at the Philharmonic as if it were jazz.
That's what he was doing.
